newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GERMANY REMAINS COMMITTED TO HELP C.EUROPE - WAIGEL.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY REMAINS COMMITTED TO HELP C.EUROPE - WAIGEL.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Friday praised Hungary's first steps in cutting inflation but said the anti-inflation fight can be successful only if the reforms are consistently implemented.

"Inflation is still high, although the first steps to beat inflation have been taKen," Waigel told a one-day Hungarian-German business forum, organised jointly by Deutsche Telekom AG and the Konrad Adenauer Foundation.

"Inflation can be beaten effectively only if the reforms still ahead are implemented," he said. "Structural reforms of the social systems and administration....are inevitable to stabilise Hungary's state household."
Germany will continue to give support to the countries of the region in their reforms, he said.
"Germany continues to remain ready to help Hungary's market reforms and the similar steps of other central- and east European countries with adequate measures," Waigel said.

Since the end of 1989 Germany's support to central- and eastern Europe has amounted to 50 billion marks and another 109 billion marks for the countries of the former Soviet Union, he said, adding that this made Germany's contribution the greatest of all western countries.
According to Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development figures, he said, Germany's accounts for more than 50 percent of all financial support offered to the region.
Despite this, Waigel said, the European integration of countries like Hungary were even more important than financial support and progress was already being made.
"The first successful signs of the EU's integration policy can already be tracked," he said. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary have chances to improve their market access," he said.
Sixty-five percent of Hungary's exports go to EU member countries which account for 80 percent of Hungary's currency revenues in tourism.
The opening up of market has, however, also had been beneficial for EU countries.
"The proportion of EU exports to the Visegrad-countries within total EU exports rose to two percent from 0.58 percent," Waigel said.
